You are a programming expert. 
You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From c66234cfedfc3e6e3b62563a5f2c1562be09a35d Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: John Keeping <john@metanate.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Jan 2018 16:01:04 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] ASoC: rockchip: i2s: fix playback after runtime resume

When restoring registers during runtime resume, we must not write to
I2S_TXDR which is the transmit FIFO as this queues up a sample to be
output and pushes all of the output channels down by one.

This can be demonstrated with the speaker-test utility:

	for i in a b c; do speaker-test -c 2 -s 1; done

which should play a test through the left speaker three times but if the
I2S hardware starts runtime suspended the first sample will be played
through the right speaker.

Fix this by marking I2S_TXDR as volatile (which also requires marking it
as readble, even though it technically isn't).  This seems to be the
most robust fix, the alternative of giving I2S_TXDR a default value is
more fragile since it does not prevent regcache writing to the register
in all circumstances.

While here, also fix the configuration of I2S_RXDR and I2S_FIFOLR; these
are not writable so they do not suffer from the same problem as I2S_TXDR
but reading from I2S_RXDR does suffer from a similar problem.

Fixes: f0447f6cbb20 ("ASoC: rockchip: i2s: restore register during runtime_suspend/resume cycle", 2016-09-07)
Signed-off-by: John Keeping <john@metanate.com>
Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org

diff --git a/sound/soc/rockchip/rockchip_i2s.c b/sound/soc/rockchip/rockchip_i2s.c
index 908211e1d6fc..eb27f6c24bf7 100644
--- a/sound/soc/rockchip/rockchip_i2s.c
+++ b/sound/soc/rockchip/rockchip_i2s.c
@@ -504,6 +504,7 @@ static bool rockchip_i2s_rd_reg(struct device *dev, unsigned int reg)
 	case I2S_INTCR:
 	case I2S_XFER:
 	case I2S_CLR:
+	case I2S_TXDR:
 	case I2S_RXDR:
 	case I2S_FIFOLR:
 	case I2S_INTSR:
@@ -518,6 +519,9 @@ static bool rockchip_i2s_volatile_reg(struct device *dev, unsigned int reg)
 	switch (reg) {
 	case I2S_INTSR:
 	case I2S_CLR:
+	case I2S_FIFOLR:
+	case I2S_TXDR:
+	case I2S_RXDR:
 		return true;
 	default:
 		return false;
@@ -527,6 +531,8 @@ static bool rockchip_i2s_volatile_reg(struct device *dev, unsigned int reg)
 static bool rockchip_i2s_precious_reg(struct device *dev, unsigned int reg)
 {
 	switch (reg) {
+	case I2S_RXDR:
+		return true;
 	default:
 		return false;
 	}
-- 
2.25.1

### Summary of Modifications

#### Modifications in `rockchip_i2s.c`
1. **Marking Registers as Volatile**: 
   - The register `I2S_TXDR` has been marked as volatile to prevent writing to it during runtime resume, which could incorrectly affect playback by queuing samples and shifting audio output channels. This change safeguards against unintended behavior and ensures proper audio output.
   - `I2S_FIFOLR` has also been marked as volatile, though it is not writable, this aligns with the behavioral protection strategy applied to `I2S_TXDR`.
   
2. **Updating Read and Write Checks**:
   - The function `rockchip_i2s_rd_reg` now includes `I2S_TXDR` to the list of registers that can be checked for reads.
   - The function `rockchip_i2s_volatile_reg` includes `I2S_FIFOLR`, `I2S_TXDR`, and `I2S_RXDR` as volatile registers, ensuring the system handles their state correctly during runtime operations.

3. **Precious Register Handling**: 
   - The function `rockchip_i2s_precious_reg` includes `I2S_RXDR` as a precious register, which prevents unwanted writes and ensures its state is preserved correctly.

#### Relationships Between Modifications
The modifications are all coordinated around fixing the audio playback issue that occurs when the I2S device resumes from a runtime suspended state. By marking `I2S_TXDR` as volatile, the patch prevents direct writes that could disrupt the audio stream. The changes to `I2S_FIFOLR` and `I2S_RXDR` ensure that the register handling logic remains robust against similar issues during read and write operations. This collective adjustment enhances the stability and reliability of audio playback in the system during power state transitions.

Here is the commit message:
ASoC: rockchip: i2s: fix playback after runtime resume

When restoring registers during runtime resume, we must not write to
I2S_TXDR which is the transmit FIFO as this queues up a sample to be
output and pushes all of the output channels down by one.

This can be demonstrated with the speaker-test utility:

	for i in a b c; do speaker-test -c 2 -s 1; done

which should play a test through the left speaker three times but if the
I2S hardware starts runtime suspended the first sample will be played
through the right speaker.

Fix this by marking I2S_TXDR as volatile (which also requires marking it
as readble, even though it technically isn't).  This seems to be the
most robust fix, the alternative of giving I2S_TXDR a default value is
more fragile since it does not prevent regcache writing to the register
in all circumstances.

While here, also fix the configuration of I2S_RXDR and I2S_FIFOLR; these
are not writable so they do not suffer from the same problem as I2S_TXDR
but reading from I2S_RXDR does suffer from a similar problem.

Fixes: f0447f6cbb20 ("ASoC: rockchip: i2s: restore register during runtime_suspend/resume cycle", 2016-09-07)
Signed-off-by: John Keeping <john@metanate.com>
Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org

Here is the root cause:
The bug arises from writing to the `I2S_TXDR` register during the runtime resume process, which inadvertently queues up an audio sample. This causes the playback to shift, leading to audio being played through the wrong output channel, especially if the I2S hardware was previously suspended. The absence of appropriate checks on the write operations allowed this behavior, resulting in incorrect audio output.

Here is the patch:
 
 static bool rockchip_i2s_rd_reg(struct device *dev, unsigned int reg)
 {
 	switch (reg) {
 	case I2S_TXCR:
 	case I2S_RXCR:
 	case I2S_CKR:
 	case I2S_DMACR:
 	case I2S_INTCR:
 	case I2S_XFER:
 	case I2S_CLR:
+	case I2S_TXDR:
 	case I2S_RXDR:
 	case I2S_FIFOLR:
 	case I2S_INTSR:
 		return true;
 	default:
 		return false;
 	}
 }
 
 static bool rockchip_i2s_volatile_reg(struct device *dev, unsigned int reg)
 {
 	switch (reg) {
 	case I2S_INTSR:
 	case I2S_CLR:
+	case I2S_FIFOLR:
+	case I2S_TXDR:
+	case I2S_RXDR:
 		return true;
 	default:
 		return false;
 	}
 }
 
 static bool rockchip_i2s_precious_reg(struct device *dev, unsigned int reg)
 {
 	switch (reg) {
+	case I2S_RXDR:
+		return true;
 	default:
 		return false;
 	}
 }

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c

+	case I2S_RXDR:
```
Reason:
The fix involves marking `I2S_TXDR` (and `I2S_RXDR`) as volatile. By doing this, it prevents any unintended writes to `I2S_TXDR` during the runtime resume process, thus stopping the queuing of audio samples that cause channel shift and ensuring that register writes are managed correctly in all circumstances.
